Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:10:1.english: Which is not so in [the case of] fire - As [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:11:1.english: An ember - Which does not burn unless [he] fanned it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:12:1.hebrew: שלהבת - שמסר אור מלובה לחרש, דפטור? בתמיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:12:1.english: A flame - [That] he handed over a stoked fire to a deaf-mute, [and] that he is exempt?! [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:12:2.english: But didn't Reish Lakish say - In [the chapter] "HaKones Tzon LaDir" (below, Bava Kamma 59b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:12:3.hebrew: לא שנו - דהשולח הבעירה ביד חרש, שוטה וקטן, דפטור מדיני אדם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:12:3.english: They taught [this] only - [This refers to the ruling] that one who sends a fire in the hand of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor is exempt under human laws.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:12:4.english: Only when he handed him the ember and he fanned it - The deaf-mute [fanned] it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:12:5.hebrew: ברי הזיקא - מבורר הזיקו לכל, שהיא מזומנת להזיק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:12:5.english: The damage is certain - Its damage is evident to all, as it is poised to cause damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:14:1.hebrew: שור דרכיה לנתוקי - והוה ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה, שאפילו אין החרש מתירו, סופו להתיר את עצמו, הלכך שמירה רעועה היא, ואפילו התירו חרש חייב בעל השור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:14:1.english: An ox is prone to break loose - And [the owner] should have considered that even if the deaf-mute does not untie it, it will eventually untie itself. Therefore, this is an inadequate safeguarding, and even if the deaf-mute untied it, the owner of the ox is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:14:2.hebrew: לנתורי - לנפול, הלכך שמירה רעה היא, אפילו גילהו חרש, בעל הבור חייב לשלם, שלא שמרו כראוי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:14:2.english: To become dislodged - [Meaning] to fall. Therefore, this is an inadequate safeguarding; even if the deaf-mute uncovered it, the owner of the pit is liable to pay, because he did not safeguard it properly.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:14:3.hebrew: מעמיא עמיא ואזלא - ומאי דליבה חרש, לא רמיא עליה דבעל גחלת לאסוקי אדעתיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:14:3.english: It progressively dims - And that which the deaf-mute fanned [it], it was not incumbent upon the owner of the ember to anticipate [this].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:15:1.hebrew: ולרבי יוחנן דאמר - בהכונס, אפילו מסר לו שלהבת פטור, דהשתא מוקי להא דקתני מה שאין כן באש בשלהבת, ודכוותיה דמחייב גבי שור ובור בשור מותר ובור מגולה, מאי שנא כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:15:1.english: And according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said - In [chapter] HaKones, [that] even if he handed him a flame, he is exempt; for now, [the Gemara] establishes that which [the baraita] teaches, "which is not the case with fire," as [referring to] a flame, and the corresponding case where he is liable regarding an ox and a pit [is] with an untethered ox and an uncovered pit — [so the Gemara asks,] "What is different, etc.?"

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:16:2.hebrew: צבתא דחרש קגרים - אחיזתו של חרש גרמה ההבער, שהוא נטלה והוליכה לגדיש. הכא, לא צבתא דחרש קגרים, שהשור הלך והזיק, וכן הבור, ולא על ידי חרש הזיק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:16:2.english: The deaf-mute's holding caused [the damage] - The deaf-mute's holding caused the burning, for he took it and carried it to the stack of grain. Here, the deaf-mute's holding did not cause [the damage], for the ox went and caused damage, and so too the pit, and it was not through the deaf-mute that it caused damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:16:3.hebrew: צבתא - אחיזתו וכחו, מלשון צבתא שקורין טניילא"ש. ל"א גרס' צוותא: יחודו של חרש, שנתייחד עם השלהבת ונטלה, ולשון צוותא שולא"ש, כדאמרינן: ליהוי צוותא לחברו (ב"ב דף כא.):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:16:3.english: Holding - His holding and his force, from the term tzavta [tongs], which they call tenailles [in Old French]. Another version reads tzavta [צוותא]: The deaf-mute's being alone [with the flame], in that he was alone with the flame and took it; and the term tzavta means solas [company in Old French], as we say: "Let him be company for his fellow" (Bava Batra 21a).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:18:1.english: Ransom - In [the case of] a forewarned [ox] that killed a free person.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:18:2.hebrew: אסור בהנאה - אם המית אדם, כדכתיב: "ובעל השור נקי", כאדם שאומר לחבירו: "פלוני יצא נקי מנכסיו", ואין לו בהן הנאה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:18:2.english: Forbidden to derive benefit - If it killed a person, as it is written: "And the owner of the ox shall be clear" [Exodus 21:28], like a person who says to his fellow: "So-and-so came out clean of his property," and he has no benefit from them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:18:3.hebrew: מה שאין כן בבור - שאין בעל הבור חייב בתשלומי מיתת אדם, כדאמרינן: "שור ולא אדם":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:18:3.english: Which is not so in [the case of] a pit - For the owner of the pit is not liable for payment for the death of a person, as we say: "An ox," and not a person.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:1:1.english: One-third of his estate - That a person is obligated to spend one-third of what he has on the mitzva of a lulav, or tzitzit, or a Torah scroll.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:2:1.hebrew: בהידור מצוה עד שליש במצוה - שאם מוצא ב' ספרי תורות לקנות, ואחד הדור מחבירו, יוסיף שליש הדמים ויקח את ההדור. דתניא (שבת דף קלג:): זה אלי ואנוהו — התנאה לפניו במצות: עשה לך ספר תורה נאה, לולב נאה, טלית נאה, ציצית נאה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:2:1.english: For the embellishment of a mitzvah, up to one-third of the mitzvah - That if one finds two Torah scrolls to buy, and one is more beautiful than the other, he should add one-third of the price and take the more beautiful one. For it is taught in a baraita (Shabbat 133b): "This is my God and I will glorify Him" [Exodus 15:2] — beautify yourself before Him with mitzvot: make for yourself a beautiful Torah scroll, a beautiful lulav, a beautiful tallit, [and] beautiful tzitzit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:3:1.hebrew: שליש מלגיו - וכגון אם הקטן נמכר בששה, יוסיף שני דינרי, דהיינו שליש מלגיו, שליש שבתוך הדמים, ויקח את ההדור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:3:1.english: One-third from within - For example, if the smaller [item] is sold for six [dinars], he adds two dinars, which is one-third from within, [meaning] a third that is within the price, and purchases the splendid [one].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:3:2.hebrew: או שליש מלבר - הדמים יחלוק לשנים, ויוסיף חלק שלישי משלו, דהיינו: אם קטן נמכר בששה, יוסיף שלשה דינרין, ויקח את הגדול בתשעה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:3:2.english: Or a third from without - He divides the price into two and adds a third part of his own; that is, if a small [item] is sold for six [dinars], he adds three dinars and purchases the large [item] for nine.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:4:1.hebrew: עד שליש משלו - דהיינו אותו שליש שיוסיף בהידור מצוה, משלו הוא, שאינו נפרע לו בחייו, כדאמרינן: "היום לעשותם, ולא היום ליטול שכרם" (ע"ז דף ג.):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:4:1.english: Up to one-third is from his own - That is, that one-third that he adds to embellish the mitzva is from his own [finances], for it is not reimbursed to him during his lifetime, as we say: "Today to perform them, and not today to receive their reward" (Avodah Zarah 3a).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:4:2.hebrew: מכאן ואילך - מה שיוסיף בהידור יותר על שליש, יפרע לו הקב"ה בחייו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:4:2.english: From this point forward - Whatever he adds for beautification beyond one-third, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will repay him in his lifetime.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:5:1.english: That I was obligated in its safeguarding - That I became obligated to safeguard it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:5:2.hebrew: הכשרתי את נזקו - כלומר: אם הזיק, הכשרתי וזימנתי אותו היזק, שלא שמרתיו יפה. כך מצאתי. לישנא אחרינא: הכשרתי את נזקו - עלי להכשיר ולתקן את נזקו, כלומר: אני חייב לשלם. מפי מורי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:5:2.english: I facilitated its damage - That is to say, if it caused damage, [it is as though] I facilitated and brought about that damage, in that I did not guard it properly. So I found [written]. Another version: "I facilitated its damage" — it is upon me to make fit and repair its damage; that is to say, I am obligated to pay. [Received] from the mouth of my teacher.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:5:3.hebrew: הכשרתי במקצת נזקו חבתי בתשלומי כו' - האי הכשרתי לא דמיא להכשרתי קמא, דהא ודאי זימנתי הוא. כלומר: אם זימנתי את מקצת נזקו, אע"פ שלא זימנתיו כולו, חבתי לשלם את נזקו כהכשר כל נזקו, כאלו זימנתיו כולו. ובגמרא מפרש היכי דמי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:5:3.english: I facilitated part of its damage, I am liable for payments, etc. - This [instance of] "I facilitated" is not similar to the first "I facilitated", for this [one] is certainly [in the sense of] "I brought about." That is to say: if I brought about part of its damage, even though I did not bring about all of it, I am liable to pay for its damage like the facilitating of all of its damage — as if I had brought about all of it. And in the Gemara it explains what this is like.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:6:1.hebrew: נכסים שאין בהם מעילה - כלומר, אם הזקתי נכסים שאין בהן מעילה אני חייב לשלם, אבל אם הזקתי נכסי הקדש איני חייב, דנפקא לן כולהו נזקין משור רעהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:6:1.english: Property that is not subject to [the prohibition of] misuse - That is to say, if I damaged property that is not subject to [the prohibition of] misuse, I am liable to pay, but if I damaged consecrated property, I am not liable, for we derive all [categories of] damage from "the ox of his fellow."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:6:2.hebrew: של בני ברית - לאפוקי נכרי, דאינו חייב בנזקיו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:6:2.english: Of members of the covenant - To exclude a gentile, for [one] is not liable for damage [caused to] his [property].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:6:3.hebrew: ונכסים המיוחדים - שיש להם בעלים, לאפוקי דהפקר, שאם הזקתי נכסים דהפקר, פטור, ובגמרא מפרש לה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:6:3.english: And designated property - [Property] that has an owner, to exclude ownerless [property], for if I damaged ownerless property, [I am] exempt, and in the Gemara it explains it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:7:1.hebrew: ובכל מקום - חב המזיק, כמו שהזיקו נכסיו את נכסי בני הברית ואת נכסיו המיוחדין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:7:1.english: And in any place - The damager is liable, just as [when] his property damaged the property of members of the covenant and his [the injured party's] designated property.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:7:2.hebrew: חוץ מרשות המיוחדת למזיק - שאם נכנס שורו של ניזק ברשות המזיק, והזיקו שור של מזיק, פטור, דאמר ליה: תורך ברשותי מאי בעי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:7:2.english: Except for a domain designated for the damager - For if the ox of the injured party entered the domain of the damager, and the ox of the damager injured it, [the damager] is exempt, for he can say to him: "What is your ox doing in my domain?"

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:8:1.english: And the domain of the injured party and the damaging party - It is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:9:1.hebrew: כשהזיק חב המזיק - הא דרשינן ליה בריש פירקין לאתויי קרן, וכשהזיק חב המזיק דרישא לא דרשינן ליה, דלאו יתירה היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 9b:9:1.english: When [it] causes damage, the damager is liable - This [phrase] we expound at the beginning of our chapter to include Keren [goring], and "when [it] causes damage, the damager is liable" of the first [mishna] we do not expound, because it is not superfluous.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:11:1.hebrew: בשור קשור ובור מכוסה - פי': כראוי, דאי בשלא כראוי, לאו כלום היא. ועוד, מדפריך: מ"ש הכא, כלומר: ובשניהם היה להם ליפטור, מדהדר מוקי לה בשור מותר ובור מגולה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:11:1.english: With a tethered ox and a covered pit - Explanation: Properly [tethered and covered]; for if [it were done] improperly, that is nothing [i.e., of no effect]. And furthermore, [this is proven] from the fact that [the Gemara] objects: "What is different here [and what is different there]?" — that is to say: in both of them they should be exempt — since it subsequently establishes it with an untethered ox and an exposed pit.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:14:1.hebrew: שור עביד לנתוקי - פרש"י: אפי' בלא חרש דרכו לנתוקי מאליו, וכן בור דרכו לנתורי מאליו. וקשה: דע"כ בקשרו ובכסהו כראוי מיירי, כדפירש, ולקמן (בבא קמא דף נב.) תנן: כסהו כראוי, פטור. ונראה לפרש: דדרכו לנתוקי ע"י חרש קאמר, דגרע משום דמסר לחרש; אבל גחלת לא גרע כ"כ, דאין דרכו ללבות גחלת כמו שדרכו לנתוקי שור ולנתורי בור, דכמה דשביק לה חרש, מעמיא עמיא ואזיל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:14:1.english: An ox is prone to break loose - Rashi explained: Even without a deaf-mute, its way is to break loose on its own, and likewise a pit, its way is to fall in on its own. And this is difficult: For perforce we are dealing with [a case where] he tied it and covered it properly, as explained; and later (Bava Kamma 52a) we learned: "[If] he covered it properly, he is exempt." And it seems [correct] to explain that [the Gemara] means: "its way is to break loose through a deaf-mute" — that it is worsened because he handed it over to a deaf-mute. But an ember is not worsened so much, for it is not his [the deaf-mute's] way to fan an ember as it is his way to untie an ox and to dislodge [the cover of] a pit, for as long as the deaf-mute leaves it alone, it progressively dims.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:15:1.hebrew: ולרבי יוחנן דאמר אפי' מסר לו שלהבת פטור כו' - תימה: מאי קשה ליה? הא שלהבת לרבי יוחנן כמו גחלת לר"ל, ובשור קשור ובור מכוסה יכול להעמידו, ומשום דחרש עביד לנתוקי ולנתורי, כמו שאמר לר"ל! וי"ל: דמשמע ליה דטעמא דרבי יוחנן דפטר משום שהקטן שומרו, ואין הקטן עושה היזק אלא אדרבה עושה שמירה. והשתא ניחא, דלא תיקשי לרבי יוחנן דמוקי לה בשור מותר ובור מגולה: אמאי נקט שמסרו לחש"ו? והא בלא מסרו נמי חייב! דנקט מסרו לרבותא, אע"פ שעשה שמירה קצת. ובהאי סברא פליג אריש לקיש:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:15:1.english: And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says [that] even [if] he handed over a flame, he is exempt, etc. - It is astonishing: What is difficult to it [the Gemara]? Behold, a flame according to Rabbi Yoḥanan is like an ember according to Reish Lakish, and [the Gemara] could establish it regarding a tethered ox and a covered pit, and [explain that it is] because a deaf-mute is prone to untie [the ox] and dislodge [the pit cover], just as it said according to Reish Lakish! And one can say that it understood that the reason of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who exempts, is because the minor guards it, and the minor does not cause damage, but rather on the contrary, provides guarding. And now it is well, so that there is no difficulty for Rabbi Yoḥanan, who establishes it regarding an untethered ox and an uncovered pit: Why did [the Baraita] specify that he handed it over to a deaf-mute, an idiot, or a minor (chashu)? Behold, even without handing it over, he is also liable! [Rather,] it specified "he handed it over" to teach a novelty: even though he performed a bit of guarding [by handing it to him, he is still liable]. And in this reasoning he disagrees with Reish Lakish.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:17:1.hebrew: חומר בשור - האי שור היינו קרן, כדמוכח בכולה שמעתין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:17:1.english: A stringency in [the case of] an ox - This "ox" is horn (keren), as is proven throughout our entire discussion.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:18:1.hebrew: ודרכו לילך ולהזיק - הא דלא חשיב שהוא בעלי חיים, מה שאין כן בבור, משום דהוי בכלל ודרכו לילך ולהזיק. וכוונתו להזיק לא שייך למתני גבי בור, שאין בעלי חיים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:18:1.english: And its manner is to go and cause damage - That which [the Tanna] did not count that it is a living creature (ba'alei chayim), which is not the case with a pit, is because this is included in "and its manner is to go and cause damage." And "its intent is to damage" is not applicable to teach regarding a pit, which is not a living creature.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:18:2.hebrew: מה שאין כן בבור - שאין משלם כופר. וכן אש, דקתני בסמוך: משא"כ באש. וא"ת: ונילף משור, ונחייבו בכופר? ואף על גב דאיכא למימר שכן ב"ח — דהא מסקינן לקמן בפרק כיצד (בבא קמא דף כו.) דאיכא כופר ברגל, שמע מינה דילפינן רגל מקרן, ולא פרכינן: מה לקרן שכן כוונתו להזיק וחייב ברה"ר. ויש לומר: דאש ובור פטורין, דדרשינן: עליו — ולא על בור, עליו — ולא על האש, כדדרשינן לקמן בסוף כיצד (שם): עליו — ולא על האדם. וא"ת: שור ולא אדם דכתיב בבור, למ"ל? ת"ל מעליו! ויש לומר: דאיצטריך שור ולא אדם לפטור עבד שנפל בתוכו, או עובד כוכבים הקנוי לישראל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:18:2.english: Which is not the case for pit - That [the owner] does not pay ransom (kofer). And similarly fire, as [the Baraita] teaches nearby: "Which is not the case for fire." And if you say: Let us derive [them] from ox, and obligate them in ransom (kofer)! And even though one could say: [Ox is different] in that it is a living creature (ba'alei chayyim) — for behold, we conclude later in the chapter "Keitsad" (Bava Kamma 26a) that there is ransom (kofer) for foot (regel); deduce from it that we derive foot from horn (keren), and we do not refute [it by arguing]: What about horn? For its intention is to cause damage, and it is liable in the public domain! And one can say that fire and pit are exempt because we expound: "Upon it" (alav) — and not upon pit; "upon it" — and not upon fire; just as we expound later at the end of "Keitsad" (ibid.): "Upon it" — and not upon man. And if you say: [The exclusion of] "an ox" and not a person, which is written regarding pit, why do I need it? Let it be derived from "upon it"! And one can say that "an ox and not a person" was necessary to exempt [the owner from liability for] a slave who fell into it, or a gentile acquired by an Israelite.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:1:1.hebrew: אילימא שליש ביתו - משמע דאין צריך לבזבז כל ממונו לקנות אתרוג, אפילו לא ימצא בפחות והויא מצוה עוברת. ואפילו שליש ביתו משמע דלא מחייב. ואמרינן נמי (כתובות דף נ.): המבזבז אל יבזבז יותר מחומש. ובסוכה (דף מא:) חשיב ליה רבותא דר"ג, שקנה אתרוג באלף זוז:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:1:1.english: If we say a third of his estate - This implies that one is not required to spend all his wealth to purchase an etrog, even if he cannot find [one] for less and it is a passing mitzvah (mitzvah overet). And it implies that he is not even obligated [to spend] a third of his estate. And we also say (Ketubot 50a): "One who spends should not spend more than a fifth." And in Sukkah (41b), it considers it a remarkable feat of Rabban Gamliel that he purchased an etrog for one thousand zuz.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:1:2.hebrew: אילו איתרמיא ליה - אפילו מיירי בעשורייתא דרבי, כדאשכחן בפרק מציאת האשה (כתובות דף סח.), מ"מ ידוע שלא היה חייב לבזבז כל כך:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:1:2.english: If [three mitzvot] happened to present themselves to him - Even if [the Gemara] is dealing with [a calculation like] Rabbi's tenths [where each is taken from what remains], as we find in the chapter "Metziat HaIsha" (Ketubot 68a), nevertheless it is known that he would not be obligated to squander so much.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:2:1.hebrew: עד שליש במצוה - פירוש: שאם מצא אתרוג כאגוז, כמו ששיערו חכמים, ואחד גדול ממנו שליש, יקנהו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:2:1.english: Up to a third in the mitzvah - Explanation: That if one found an etrog [the size of] a nut, as the Sages quantified, and another [that is] one-third larger than it, he should buy it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:4:1.hebrew: משל הקב"ה - אוכל פירות בעוה"ז, והקרן קיימת לו לעוה"ב:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 9b:4:1.english: From the Holy One, Blessed be He - [He] eats the fruits in this world, and the principal remains for him for the World-to-Come.
